summary_short: A 99-year-old British woman claimed the world's oldest wing-walker title—just months after her niece saw another gran achieve it and encouraged her to try.
body:
When Helga Duffy's niece, Jackie Rose, saw news reports this year about 97-year-old Betty Bromage becoming the world's oldest wing-walker, she thought of her aunt. The staff at Helga's assisted-living facility agreed it was worth suggesting. Helga had no idea what wing-walking even was, but at 99, she decided it was time to do something different. This week, Guinness World Records officially recognized her as the new record-holder after she completed the stunt at Rendcomb Airfield in Gloucestershire, England—just three months after Betty's achievement.

Despite arthritis and a painful right knee, Helga spent over five minutes strapped to the top of a small aircraft. The former nurse described the experience as transformative. Once the plane climbed to a thousand meters, she took three deep breaths and felt, as she put it, "so good" she wondered if it resembled the effects of drugs. "The air up there is so pure you wouldn't believe it," she recalled. She felt secure throughout, and when she landed, an official Guinness World Records adjudicator presented her with a certificate.

What makes Helga's record remarkable isn't just the age—it's what it represents. Jackie told the BBC she wanted to prove that "even though she's 99, she's still that lady she was years and years ago." Betty Bromage took the news in stride, joking that she planned to turn 100 and reclaim the title. Helga's stunt also raised over £1,600 for the regional Air Ambulance charity. Her message to others: "Try anything. Don't ever say, 'I can't do it'. You can't 'see' until you've tried." The certificate now hangs in her care facility—a reminder that age is just a number.
quick_facts: Helga Duffy, 99, is the world's oldest wing-walker
Record set at Rendcomb Airfield in Gloucestershire, England
Broke previous record held by 97-year-old Betty Bromage
